first.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ, directly matching the documented effect in memory_86 (shortening onboarding lifts completion and time-to-value) and memory_31 (signup simplification lifts activation). This is a low-risk, mechanism-consistent fix for a metric that is currently declining, and it strengthens the funnel without competing on price. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is tempting given the competitor's aggressive entry pricing, but that memory reports acquisition/revenue lift without clear evidence on long-term qualified-revenue quality or margin durability — matching price cuts risks a race-to-the-bottom that could damage sustainable qualified revenue, the stated primary objective. I'm verifying memory_86 to confirm the onboarding effect still holds and applies to the current self-serve population, and memory_73 to check whether the original record shows any signal about customer quality/retention degradation before ruling pricing out. Given only one experiment slot, I favor the safer, metric-aligned onboarding fix over a reactive pricing match whose downstream value risk is unresolved. This is a standard experiment (not broad rollout) since we haven't yet confirmed durability under current conditions with post-verification data.
